studies.label: Experiment 2: open-ended logo generation

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 47, Appendix C.5, final analyzed sample; arm counts are in PDF p. 36, Table A.2, sample-size note, quoted in estimate sources
counts_source.quote: Our final sample thus included 1,857 participants and 18,425 prompts.

arms.name: DALL-E 2
arms.description: Participant prompts passed directly to the earlier image-generation model, without intermediate rewriting (PDF p. 9, section 3.1). Analyzed count: PDF p. 36, Table A.2.

arms.name: DALL-E 3 (Verbatim)
arms.description: A hidden prefix asked GPT-4 to leave the participant prompt unchanged before image generation. Rewriting was reduced but was not eliminated (PDF p. 38, Appendix B.2). Analyzed count: PDF p. 36, Table A.2.

arms.name: DALL-E 3 (Revised)
arms.description: The default DALL-E 3 endpoint, including hidden GPT-4 prompt rewriting that adds detail or restructures the prompt (PDF p. 9, section 3.1; PDF p. 38, Appendix B.2). Analyzed count: PDF p. 36, Table A.2.

studies.task: Iteratively prompt the assigned image generator to create the best original logo for a randomly assigned hypothetical client brief, with at least 10 attempts within 25 minutes (PDF p. 41, Appendix B.5.1–B.5.2).

ai_tool.name: OpenAI DALL-E 2; DALL-E 3 (Verbatim); DALL-E 3 (Revised), with GPT-4 for system-side prompt rewriting
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 9, section 3.1; PDF p. 38, Appendix B.2. Model release years are not stated. The logo experiment was conducted in 2025 (PDF p. 43, Appendix B.5.3); this is not used as a model release year.

preregistration.where: PDF p. 43, Appendix B.5.4, states that the study was preregistered but replaces the URL with "URL removed to maintain anonymity". PDF p. 66, Appendix I, says the logo-task preregistered hypotheses were limited to main-text analyses.

estimates.outcome: Logo design quality / fulfillment of the client brief (Bradley–Terry strength)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Within each client brief, gpt-4.1-nano judged which of two original or replayed logos better fulfilled the client requirements; image order was randomized. Maximum-likelihood Bradley–Terry strengths were fitted to the resulting win–loss matrices, providing a continuous quality score per logo (PDF pp. 49–50, Appendix D.2). The treatment analysis uses these output scores, not individual judging pairs; logo images were not resampled repeatedly per prompt (PDF p. 12, section 3.3.1).

stats.difference_is: The reported regression coefficient is the adjusted treatment-minus-control ATE in raw Bradley–Terry strength units; it is not an unadjusted arm-mean difference.

regression.model: Pairwise linear regression of output-level Bradley–Terry strength on the assigned-model indicator, with iteration and logo-task fixed effects. Main-text ATEs use participant-clustered robust standard errors (PDF p. 58, Appendix F.2.1; PDF p. 55, Appendix F.1.1).

paper_effect.standardizer: The main-text statement calls this approximately 0.57 standard deviations but does not separately specify its denominator. Appendix E.2 (PDF pp. 53–54) describes within-task/attempt output-score normalization across the two arms; its separately reported robustness result is retained in s2_logo_quality_zscore_verbatim_vs_dalle2. No participant-level control or pooled SD is supplied.

The all-arm prompt count is not substituted for the contrast observation count. AI was available throughout output production; later scoring does not make this a delayed or after_ai outcome. Its precision is retained separately from the appendix robustness estimate. Figure 3B (PDF p. 18) displays arm means and attempt-specific effects without numerical labels; these were not read off the graph. No SE was derived from the confidence interval.

estimates.outcome: Logo design quality / fulfillment of the client brief (within-logo/attempt Z-scored Bradley–Terry strength)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Within each client brief, gpt-4.1-nano judged which of two original or replayed logos better fulfilled the client requirements; image order was randomized. Maximum-likelihood Bradley–Terry strengths were fitted to the resulting win–loss matrices, providing a continuous quality score per logo (PDF pp. 49–50, Appendix D.2). The treatment analysis uses these output scores, not individual judging pairs; logo images were not resampled repeatedly per prompt (PDF p. 12, section 3.3.1). For this robustness analysis, output scores are standardized within logo-task/attempt cells using the mean and SD across the DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 arms; Appendix E.2 states that the same normalization applies to logos (PDF pp. 53–54).

stats.difference_is: Adjusted treatment-minus-control ATE on the paper’s Z-scored output scale.

regression.model: Repetition of the overall ATE analysis using Z-scored Bradley–Terry output strengths (PDF p. 64, Appendix H.3.1), following the main analysis with iteration and logo-task fixed effects and participant-clustered uncertainty (PDF p. 58, Appendix F.2.1). Standardization uses within-logo/attempt means and SDs across both arms (PDF pp. 53–54, Appendix E.2).

estimates.notes: Counts are final analyzed people in the relevant arms from Table A.2. The paper does not print a pairwise participant total or a pairwise output observation count, so n_total and n_units are null; neither was calculated. Arm means and their SDs/SEs are not printed. The all-arm prompt count is not substituted for the contrast observation count. AI was available throughout output production; later scoring does not make this a delayed or after_ai outcome. The LLM judgment measures design quality/brief fulfillment, coded usefulness, with higher scores indicating better creative output. The preregistered primary-outcome hierarchy is not stated in the available paper. This is a robustness analysis of the same outcome, randomized people, and arm contrast as s2_logo_quality_verbatim_vs_dalle2; it is not an independent sample. The printed z denotes an effect on the standardized outcome, not a z test statistic and not Cohen’s d. The standardizer is at the output/task/attempt level across arms, not the SD of participant-average scores. The paper’s general Z-scoring rule is within task/attempt; its exception for trajectory regressions standardizes within task only. No SD or SE was inferred from the normalized score or its confidence interval.

not_extracted.what: S1: Experiment 1, fixed-target image replication, including CLIP/DreamSim fidelity, rescalings, first/average/best-attempt summaries, and its additional analyses
not_extracted.reason: This is a fixed-reference replication task rather than the eligible open-ended creative task. The reconciled screening decision excludes S1 from creativity estimates. The task and fidelity scoring are confirmed in PDF p. 10, sections 3.2–3.2.1; PDF p. 11 contrasts this task with open-ended logo creation. Appendix I is explicitly scoped to image replication (PDF p. 66). Target fidelity is not across-person output diversity.

not_extracted.what: S2: Replay-based model effect, in raw and Z-scored logo quality
not_extracted.reason: Researcher replay holds the same participants’ prompts fixed and changes the evaluation model after the task; this is the direct/model component of a mediation-like decomposition, not a contrast between separately randomized human working conditions. Excluded under the replay/model-only and mediation rules (PDF p. 19, section 4.2.2; PDF pp. 56–57, Appendix F.1.3; PDF p. 59, Appendix F.2.3; PDF p. 65, Appendix H.3.3).

not_extracted.what: S2: Replay-based prompting effect, in raw and Z-scored logo quality
not_extracted.reason: This indirect/prompting component compares original Verbatim-arm outputs with researcher replays of DALL-E 2 prompts on Verbatim. It is a decomposition of the treatment effect through prompting, rather than the original full treatment contrast, and mediation analyses are excluded (PDF p. 19, section 4.2.2; PDF pp. 56–57, Appendix F.1.3; PDF p. 59, Appendix F.2.3; PDF p. 65, Appendix H.3.3).

not_extracted.what: S2: Reverse replay of Verbatim participants’ prompts on DALL-E 2, in raw and Z-scored logo quality
not_extracted.reason: One side consists of counterfactual images generated by the researchers after human participation. Participants were not assigned to work in this replay configuration, so it is not an additional eligible AI-assistance contrast (PDF p. 13, section 3.4; PDF p. 19, section 4.2.2; PDF p. 65, Appendix H.3.3).

not_extracted.what: S2: Distributional/quantile effects and interactions in Table 2
not_extracted.reason: These estimate heterogeneity by realized outcome percentile, a post-treatment rank, and include decomposition components. The un-interacted coefficient is conditional on the lowest percentile rather than a full-sample ATE. They measure dispersion of quality, not content similarity across people (PDF p. 21, Table 2 and note; PDF pp. 57–58, Appendix F.1.4; PDF p. 59, Appendix F.2.4).

not_extracted.what: S2: Attempt-by-model trajectory regressions, raw and Z-scored logo quality
not_extracted.reason: The interaction coefficients assess moderation by attempt number. Their model-indicator coefficients are conditional on iteration zero and are not overall ATEs. The full-sample ATEs are extracted separately; no effect was calculated from trajectory coefficients (PDF p. 55, Equation 12; PDF p. 58, Appendix F.2.1; PDF p. 65, Appendix H.3.2).

not_extracted.what: Prompt length, in words or characters
not_extracted.reason: Measures the input supplied to the model, not elaboration or creativity of the generated logo (PDF p. 50, Appendix D.3; PDF p. 59, Appendix F.2.2).

Measures similarity between one participant’s successive input prompts, not creativity of produced images or similarity between different people’s outputs (PDF p. 50, Appendix D.4; PDF p. 59, Appendix F.2.2).

not_extracted.what: Aggregate prompt similarity / dispersion around a participant’s own prompt centroid
not_extracted.reason: A within-person input-strategy measure; it is neither diversity across people’s creative outputs nor output-scored flexibility (PDF pp. 50–51, Appendix D.4; PDF p. 59, Appendix F.2.2).
String similarity between successive input prompts, not a scored creative-output outcome (PDF p. 51, Appendix D.5).
An input-reuse behavior, not creativity or diversity scored on generated outputs (PDF p. 51, Appendix D.6).
Describes input text, including the proportion of nouns and adjectives, rather than the quality or originality of generated logos (PDF p. 51, Appendix D.7; PDF p. 59, Appendix F.2.2).

not_extracted.what: Strategic shifts / topical transitions in prompting
not_extracted.reason: Measures changes in a participant’s input strategy. Cross-prompt similarities define a threshold for that behavior; they are not an across-person creative-output diversity outcome (PDF pp. 51–52, Appendix D.8).

not_extracted.what: Prompt-rewriting compliance and original-to-rewritten prompt similarity
not_extracted.reason: Manipulation/compliance measures of system-side rewriting, not creativity scored on the produced images (PDF p. 38, Appendix B.2).

not_extracted.what: Self-reported proficiency, frequency of skill use, opinions, and attitudes toward generative AI
not_extracted.reason: Survey self-reports and attitudes are excluded; they are not scored creative outputs (PDF p. 44, Appendix C.1).
The paper describes human pairwise judgments and agreement for validating the automated scoring, but reports no human-rated full-sample treatment contrast (PDF p. 12, footnote 9).

not_extracted.what: GPT-4V-generated image-replication prompts and target-difficulty calibration
not_extracted.reason: Model-only prompting and image-difficulty calibration, not a further randomized experiment in which people receive AI assistance (PDF p. 81, Appendix I.1, H8).

open_items: Assignment-stage total and per-arm randomized counts are not explicitly printed. The initial raw-data participant total in Appendix C.5 is not substituted for n_randomized (PDF p. 46).

No pairwise analysis totals or output observation counts are printed for the extracted contrasts. Arm sizes are available, but pair totals were not calculated (PDF p. 36, Table A.2; PDF p. 47, Appendix C.5).

Arm means, arm SDs/SEs, and SDs of participant-average logo quality are not printed; arm levels in Figure 3B are unlabeled. Numerical SEs for the overall ATEs are not supplied and were not derived (PDF p. 18, Figure 3B; PDF p. 58, Appendix F.2.1).

The direct configuration comparison is reported only as a percentage in Revised-relative-to-Verbatim orientation. Its denominator and CI calculation are not specified, and an absolute Verbatim-minus-Revised coefficient is not printed (PDF p. 20, section 4.2.4).
The preregistration URL is redacted, preventing confirmation of a formal primary-outcome hierarchy (PDF p. 43, Appendix B.5.4; PDF p. 66, Appendix I).
The paper promises anonymized data and replication code upon publication but provides no usable repository URL (PDF p. 8, footnote 4).
AI model release years are not stated in the paper; ai_tool.year is null. The collection year is not treated as a release year (PDF p. 38, Appendix B.2; PDF p. 43, Appendix B.5.3).
The citation record supplied with the brief identifies a later journal version. The extracted evidence is from the saved arXiv v7 PDF; differences from the journal full text have not been checked.

primary_override.reason: For S2 / with_ai / ai_design, retain the paper’s main raw overall ATE as the primary record. The Verbatim-versus-DALL-E-2 contrast is the main model-upgrade comparison; Revised is explicitly described as secondary. The within-logo/attempt Z-score result is a robustness analysis of the same sample and contrast, not another independent estimate for pooling. This selection follows the paper-main-specification rule and does not use effect size or significance.
primary_override.locator: PDF p. 34, Appendix B.1.1, discussion of the DALL-E 3 (Revised) arm; PDF p. 18, section 4.2.1, main logo ATE

notes: Independent extraction A from the supplied saved PDF. Only the eligible logo-generation study appears in studies, preserving the screening study_id S2; the fixed-target replication study S1 is listed in not_extracted. All arms provide generative AI, so all eligible contrasts are ai_design. The four estimate records consist of three direct arm contrasts and a separately reported standardized-outcome robustness analysis of the main contrast. PDF and printed page numbers coincide. All source quotes were taken from pymupdf-extracted PDF text, with whitespace normalized; quoted statistics and counts were checked against their cited pages. Numerical JSON values preserve printed decimal precision, including trailing zeroes. Bounded p-values use ASCII exponent notation for the printed powers of ten. No effect sizes, sums of arm counts, SDs, SEs, interval conversions, or reversed effects were calculated. Assignment was individual and blind, with simultaneous randomization of the model and client brief (PDF p. 9, section 3.1; PDF p. 34, Appendix B.1). The population was a US Prolific panel of fluent English speakers using desktop or laptop devices (PDF p. 43, Appendix B.5.3). The analyzed sample excludes unsuccessful/logging-error submissions, insufficient attempts, repeated identical prompts, mismatched treatment/task labels, incomplete surveys, and failed or duplicate replay records; some exclusions and the restriction to the first required attempts were post hoc (PDF pp. 46–47, Appendix C.5). No cross-person creative-output diversity or unassisted after-AI outcome is reported. Within-person prompt dispersion is an input behavior, and quality-distribution compression is not semantic homogenization. The screening form identifies no other paper sharing these participants; shared_sample is null rather than an assertion of no overlap.
